subject: AI & Agents
title: How Recommendation Engines Know What You Want
description: A 60-second lesson on How Recommendation Engines Know What You Want.

hook.text: You bought hiking boots. Now every website shows you tents, backpacks, and trail mix.

buildup.text: Recommendation engines use collaborative filtering — finding people with similar tastes.

discovery.text: If users who bought boots also bought tents, the system suggests tents to all boot buyers.

twist.text: This creates filter bubbles — you only see what the algorithm thinks you already like.

climax.text: Amazon says 35% of its revenue comes from AI recommendations.

punchline.text: The algorithm shops for you before you even start.

quiz.question: What is collaborative filtering?
options: Recommending items based on what similar users liked

details.summary: Recommendation engines analyze your behavior, preferences, and similar users to predict what you will like next. They power suggestions on shopping sites, streaming platforms, and social media.
details.whyItMatters: Recommendations shape what you buy, watch, and read. Understanding how they work reveals why you see certain content and how to break out of filter bubbles.
takeaways: Engines combine your behavior with patterns from similar users
Collaborative and content-based filtering are the main approaches
Recommendations create filter bubbles that narrow your exposure

faq.question: How do recommendation engines predict what you want?
faq.answer: They combine collaborative filtering (what similar users liked) with content-based filtering (what matches your past choices). Hybrid approaches blend both methods for better accuracy.

faq.question: Do recommendation engines limit what you discover?
faq.answer: They can create filter bubbles by showing only content matching your existing preferences. Most platforms try to balance personalization with discovery to keep users engaged.
